## New defensible units

- `WEB-051` — AU, 27 June 2023. Tshisekedi participated in the Luanda quadripartite summit; the communiqué commended his commitment to dialogue and adopted coordinated peace-process timelines. Maps 2B.1, 2B.7, 8B.1, 8B.9. [AU communiqué](https://www.peaceau.org/en/article/communique-quadripartite-summit-of-the-east-african-community-economic-community-of-central-african-states-international-conference-on-the-great-lakes-region-and-southern-african-development-community-under-the-auspices-of-the-african-union-27-june-2023)

- `WEB-052` — IMF fifth review, December 2023. Security and elections drove spending reprioritization; revenue weakness, fiscal pressure, and macroeconomic risks remained, while authorities maintained reform commitments. Maps 5B.3, 5B.7, 5B.9, 8B.6–8B.8. [IMF review](https://www.imf.org/en/publications/cr/issues/2023/12/19/democratic-republic-of-the-congo-fifth-review-under-the-extended-credit-facility-542654)

- `WEB-053` — U.S. State Department 2023 human-rights report. Documents government killings, torture, life-threatening prison conditions, arbitrary detention, weak judicial independence, corruption, and restrictions under the state of siege; also records some official investigations and prosecutions. Administration-level evidence only. Maps 3B.1, 3B.4, 3B.5, 3B.10, 4B.4, 7B.6–7B.7. [Report mirror](https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2107668.html)

- `WEB-054` — Court of Accounts/PDL-145T dispute, July 2023. BCECO’s attempt to avoid IGF oversight was challenged, highlighting audit and control risks around a $1.66 billion public program. Maps 5B.5–5B.7, 7B.6, 8B.5–8B.8. [Actualité.cd](https://actualite.cd/index.php/2023/07/19/rdc-la-cour-des-comptes-enjoint-le-bceco-de-retirer-sa-note-dinformation-adressee-aux)

- `WEB-055` — Presidential corrective instruction, August 2023. Tshisekedi directed ministers to address governance failures and auditor inaction concerning state enterprises. This is evidence of formal response, not successful enforcement or personal integrity. Maps 5B.5, 5B.7, 7B.2, 7B.6, 7B.8, 8B.6, 8B.8. [Actualité.cd](https://actualite.cd/2023/08/27/gouvernance-des-entreprises-publiques-felix-tshisekedi-sindigne-de-linaction-des)

- `WEB-056` — UNICEF, March 2023. Conflict disrupted education for approximately 750,000 children; at least 2,100 schools in North Kivu and Ituri had stopped operating. Maps 3B.7, 6B.2, 6B.3, 6B.6, 6B.10, 8B.7. [UNICEF](https://www.unicef.org/press-releases/conflict-eastern-drc-having-devastating-impact-childrens-education)

- `WEB-057` — UNICEF, August 2023. More than 31,000 suspected or confirmed cholera cases and 230 deaths occurred during the first seven months; displacement camps faced severe water and sanitation shortages. Maps 3B.7, 6B.3, 6B.6, 6B.8, 6B.10. [UNICEF](https://www.unicef.org/press-releases/children-dr-congo-facing-worst-cholera-outbreak-six-years-warns-unicef)

- `WEB-058` — DRC Voluntary National Review, 2023. Officially reports that fewer than 58% of residents had access to improved drinking water, less than 40% in rural areas, while inequality remained high and increased from a Gini coefficient of 0.52 to 0.54 between 2020 and 2022. Self-reported government evidence; use cautiously. Maps 5B.8, 5B.10, 6B.2, 6B.8, 6B.10. [VNR PDF](https://hlpf.un.org/sites/default/files/vnrs/2023/VNR%202023%20DRC%20Report_0.pdf), pp. 66, 86.

- `WEB-059` — AP, 20 December 2023. Polling opened late or not at all, machines failed, voting was extended, displaced people faced registration and access problems, and observers raised credibility concerns. Maps 4B.1, 4B.2, 4B.7, 4B.10, 8B.5, 8B.7. [AP report](https://apnews.com/article/e23f45d40e2a28a5da85f0185e3e5425)

- `WEB-060` — UNICEF humanitarian situation report, June 2023. Reports worsening cholera, nutrition, health-access, displacement, gender-based-violence, and child-protection conditions; funding gaps were above 87% in several sectors. Shared humanitarian attribution, not direct presidential conduct. Maps 3B.7, 6B.3, 6B.6, 6B.9, 8B.7, 8B.10. [UNICEF situation report](https://www.unicef.org/media/143521/file/DRC-Humanitarian-SitRep-June-2023.pdf), pp. 8–11.

## Chapter results

### 2B

The AU communiqué materially improves diplomatic attribution: Tshisekedi personally participated in the Luanda process, which commended his dialogue commitment and established coordinated political, military, humanitarian, and security timelines. The IMF review also clarifies that security and elections materially redirected fiscal spending.

Proxy-control and operational-command evidence remains unresolved. The opened sources do not establish that Tshisekedi knew of specific allied-group abuses or personally ordered unlawful operations.

### 3B

The State Department report adds precise national evidence on killings, torture, arbitrary detention, prison conditions, assembly restrictions, and limited prosecutions. It also preserves contrary evidence: some officials were investigated, prosecuted, and punished.

The evidence still does not establish prior presidential knowledge or an order for the Goma massacre. National prevalence and follow-up after the narrow command investigation remain gaps.

### 4B

The AP election report adds direct election-day logistics and access failures, including delayed openings, faulty machines, displaced-voter exclusion, and extended voting. These are strong administration-level execution evidence but do not prove presidential manipulation.

The CENI appointment chain, observer findings, and technical ambiguity around EU equipment remain the appropriate attribution limits.

### 5B

The IMF fifth review closes the previously blocked macroeconomic lead at claim level: growth remained resilient, but fiscal pressure increased as spending shifted toward security and elections, with revenue shortfalls and continuing reform risks.

The PDL-145T audit-resistance evidence strengthens the governance and execution record. Household poverty, wages, employment, inequality, and regional distribution remain only partly recoverable; official VNR inequality and water figures are useful but self-reported or not exact-year outcomes.

### 6B

UNICEF adds measurable 2023 education disruption, cholera, displacement, water, sanitation, and child-protection evidence. These materially broaden the chapter beyond maternity care and education design.

The evidence remains shared among government, conflict actors, donors, and humanitarian agencies. Mortality, learning outcomes, housing, disability outcomes, and durable social-protection delivery remain weak.

### 8B

Effectiveness evidence now covers:

- coordinated peace diplomacy;
- macroeconomic reprioritization under security and election pressure;
- PDL-145T audit and execution failures;
- election logistics and voter-access problems;
- education disruption;
- cholera and humanitarian response;
- water, sanitation, and inequality conditions.

The central conclusion remains mixed at the evidence level: formal programs and corrective instructions existed, but execution, coordination, and outcomes were uneven.
